summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727 KB payload
details: The package's `scripts.preinstall` runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub Releases (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...`) and then uses `execFileSync` to invoke the freshly downloaded Bun binary against a bundled `math_init.js` file at install time. `math_init.js` is a single-line ~727 KB script whose first construct is a string-array rotator (`function WV8StW(a,b,c){for(c=0;c<b;c++)a.push(a.shift());return a}`) over a large numeric/string table with all identifiers mangled; the launcher `setup.mjs` itself uses hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`). The package is published under `@servicetitan/mfe-quick-actions` and declares many `@servicetitan/*` dependencies, presenting as a React micro-frontend library, but its install-time behavior is unrelated to that stated purpose: fetching a second-language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated bundled payload on `npm install`. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern — the payload runs under Bun rather than Node, so Node-oriented tooling and hooks do not observe the execution — combined with an obfuscated launcher and an obfuscated payload of a size and shape with no legitimate use in a React MFE package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
